notes: This contract records Umbra's bounded non-regional IEEE 1516.1-2025 timestamped Update Attribute Values slice in the non-installable development profile. It retains recipient-specific passels and a federation-owned recipient ledger for every timestamped recipient, including immediate/nonconstrained recipients with no temporal-queue entry. The shared recipient planner selects active ordinary attribute subscriptions only; passive ordinary declarations remain retained but cannot arrange a reflection, although these timestamped cases do not independently test that selector. A legal Retract uses the Clause 8.22.3 strict timestamp condition, suppresses pending fanout, and queues Request Retraction for a recipient that already received its timestamped reflection passels. Consistent with Clause 6.10, the timestamped overload returns a designator only when the publisher is time-regulating and at least one submitted instance attribute has TSO preferred order. A one-federate regression proves that a qualifying invocation with an eligible-recipient set of zero still returns a valid public designator backed by that ledger; it covers legal Retract and later terminal classification without retaining typed attribute passels. Connection-loss regressions retain a reliable timestamp-6 passel accepted before the regulating publisher's forced resignation: one reflects it before a survivor's matching grant, a second retains it through the first of two staggered survivor deliveries until the later survivor requests and crosses time 6, and DELETE_OBJECTS collisions preserve the cutoff reflection whether the survivor was already advancing or opens the time-6 boundary after the loss; a mixed two-survivor case proves automatic cleanup remains independently gated per recipient. With asynchronous delivery enabled, bounded evoked and immediate counterparts assert reflection, matching grant, and the now-eligible receive-order automatic removal in that order within one TAR. A callback-boundary unsubscribe suppresses its reflection without leaving the accepted passel falsely pending or stranding the separately queued automatic removal. Focused alternate-advance cases exercise TARA at the defined GALT boundary, NMRA at the next queued message boundary, and FQR by flushing all queued passels while preserving reflection-before-grant ordering, payload metadata, actual grant, and optimistic floor. The evidence covers the normal non-regional path only; it does not claim timestamped Delete Object Instance, directed interactions, separate region-context Request Retraction evidence, Request Retraction behavior after FQR, generic asynchronous-delivery behavior, remote transport, package/catalog/JUnit/protected-review evidence, or conformance.
